classification: GRADED WINDOWS RESCUE RECURRENT UTILITY BUT NOT ALIGNED MEMORY
classification_rule: S2 passes the frozen recurrent-utility thresholds, but correct sequence identity is not beneficial.

next_experiment_decisions.A: YES, as a separately preregistered experiment; the graded diagnostic supports testing a full monotonic pyramid.
next_experiment_decisions.B: Use S2 as the seed geometry if a full-pyramid experiment is separately approved.
next_experiment_decisions.C: YES, under S2's frozen geometry, as a separate experiment.
next_experiment_decisions.D: YES; incremental layer-by-layer reader training is the more interpretable design if reader adaptation is approved.
next_experiment_decisions.E: DEFER; all-strictly-higher source expansion would confound the path-consistent geometry result and needs its own protocol.
next_experiment_decisions.F: YES; adapt the existing self readers before changing the source bank because recurrence helps but aligned identity remains negative.
next_experiment_decisions.G: NO; one-step recurrence must first be stable, aligned, and reproduced with any geometry-specific reader adaptation.
next_experiment_decisions.H: YES; writers remain deferred until direct-reader one-step recurrence is established.
next_experiment_decisions.I: YES; keep B1 at W=1 in the first full-pyramid experiment unless a separate protocol explicitly tests opening B1.

scientific_answers.Q1: YES: S2, S3 have positive same-window self recovery.
scientific_answers.Q10: Reduced drift does not restore correct self-sequence alignment; any positive recovery is generic recurrent utility rather than aligned memory.
scientific_answers.Q11: After separating local-window and recurrent gains, S2 is the best raw recurrence schedule and S2 is the best budget tradeoff; S2/S3 are not credited for their much larger local-KV gains.
scientific_answers.Q12: The rerun supports a material contribution from the abrupt B1-B4 receptive-field cliff only to the extent that widening windows improves same-window recurrence and representation compatibility; it does not by itself prove that geometry is the sole autonomous-loop bottleneck.
scientific_answers.Q2: Correct self sequence identity does not become beneficial for S1-S3.
scientific_answers.Q3: S2 has the highest raw same-window self recovery.
scientific_answers.Q4: S2 has the best self-recovery per low-block KV-window budget among S1-S3.
scientific_answers.Q5: Ordinary local-KV restoration contributes window-only gains of S1=+0.3050489502, S2=+0.7027291189, S3=+1.0303746836; these gains are not credited to recurrence.
scientific_answers.Q6: The extra B2-B4 readers improve B1-only self recurrence in S0, S1, S2, S3.
scientific_answers.Q7: Teacher feedback remains sequence-specific: teacher shuffled-real gaps and paired aligned wins are S0=+0.1661900824 (20/20), S1=+0.1735688344 (20/20), S2=+0.1816234028 (20/20), S3=+0.1775649507 (20/20).
scientific_answers.Q8: YES: source cosine rises and source RMS difference falls monotonically from S0 through S3.
scientific_answers.Q9: Reduced source-state drift is reported alongside recovery; it correlates with the window intervention but is not treated as a causal objective.
